style_when: the story is a single number, rule, gate or shift and restraint is the point — with no scene to photograph, the frame must still be a real assembly: a modular bay, an unlatched inspection gate, a rack of blades, an interlocking connector
prompt: A steel drum containment rack on a concrete plant floor beside a substation yard, three 55-gallon fuel drums seated in bays, a fourth bay empty, an inspection gate ajar. Graphite steel frame, safety-yellow strip, concrete grey floor. One directional key light rakes from the left across brushed steel and ribbed drum bodies, throwing long hard shadows to the right. Extreme asymmetry with the rack off-centre left and empty concrete negative space right, low three-quarter angle, hard clean edges, plain surfaces without markings.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, moulded embossed lettering, numbers
rationale: component_assembly's hard-edged modular construction lets the drum rack and an open bay state the container-count threshold directly, while nano-banana-pro renders clean steel and concrete with one directional shadow and no legible lettering. It avoids photographic clichés and the previous legible-number failure.
subject: a steel drum containment rack holding 55-gallon fuel drums, an inspection gate ajar on a concrete pad
core_thesis: Backup fuel compliance is determined by container count and tank volume, not plant size: 24 55-gallon drums reach the 1,320-gallon spill exemption ceiling.
core_conflict: self-certified spill plan vs. crossing container-count thresholds (1,320/5,000/10,000 gallons) that force PE review or the underground-tank program
composition: extreme asymmetry with the rack off-centre left and empty concrete negative space right
